questions.question: On the number line from 1 to 20, which number is directly to the left of 14?
questions.explain: On a number line, the number to the left is smaller, so directly left of 14 is 13. A common mix-up is thinking left means bigger.

questions.question: On the number line, which number is directly to the right of 8?
questions.explain: The number to the right comes after, so directly right of 8 is 9. Some kids mix up left and right and pick 7 instead.

questions.question: On the number line, 16 is to the right of 13. Which number is to the left?
questions.explain: If 16 is to the right, then 13 is to the left. Left always means the smaller number. Do not swap the two sides.

questions.question: On the number line, 9 is to the left of 14. So 14 is to the … of 9.
questions.explain: If 9 is to the left of 14, then 14 must be to the right of 9. They are the same two numbers seen from the other side.

questions.question: Sam has 13 stickers. Mia has 9 stickers. Who has more?
questions.explain: 13 is bigger than 9, so Sam has more. Some kids pick the smaller number when asked who has more.

questions.question: There are 17 red blocks and 11 blue blocks. Which colour has fewer?
questions.explain: 11 is smaller than 17, so the blue blocks are fewer. A common mix-up is picking the bigger group when asked for fewer.

questions.question: Put these numbers from smallest to biggest: 15, 9, 12.
questions.explain: Start with the smallest: 9, then 12, then 15. A common slip is going from biggest to smallest when the question asks smallest to biggest.

questions.question: You have 14 crayons. Sam has 19. Leo has 10. Put them from smallest to biggest. What is the first one?
questions.explain: From smallest to biggest: 10, 14, 19. The first one is 10. If you go backwards, you would start with 19, which is the wrong end.

questions.question: Aisha has 12 marbles. Ben has 15. Cat has 17. Put them from biggest to smallest. What is the first one?
questions.explain: From biggest to smallest: 17, 15, 12. The first one is 17. A common slip is going smallest to biggest and picking 12 instead.

questions.question: You have the numbers 8, 15, and 11. Which one is bigger than 8 but smaller than 15?
questions.explain: We need a number bigger than 8 and smaller than 15. 11 fits right in the middle. The trick is to check both ends, not just one.

questions.question: You have 14 buttons. Mia has 17. Leo has 8. Who has the most?
questions.explain: 17 is the biggest number, so Mia has the most. A common mix-up is picking the smallest number when asked for the most.

questions.question: You, Ava, and Max have 11, 17, and 6 marbles. Put them from biggest to smallest. What is the last one?
questions.explain: Biggest to smallest is 17, 11, 6, so the last one is 6. A common mix-up is ordering by the ones digit only, like putting 11 after 6 because 1 looks smaller than 6.

questions.question: Zoe starts with 14 stars and loses 3, so she has 11. Sam has 8. Who has more stars now?
questions.explain: Zoe has 11 and Sam has 8, and 11 is more than 8. The trap is looking only at the ones digit: 8 looks bigger than 1, but 11 is still more than 8.

questions.question: You, a friend, and another friend have 13, 17, and 8 coins. Put them from biggest to smallest. What is the middle one?
questions.explain: Biggest to smallest is 17, 13, 8, so the middle is 13. Watch out for grabbing the smallest (8) when the question asks for the middle.

questions.question: Max writes: 18, 12, 7. He says he put them from smallest to biggest. What went wrong?
questions.explain: 18 is the biggest and 7 is the smallest, so he went from big to small. The right order is 7, 12, 18.
